cards.title: The soak field (a page introducing an idea)
cards.does: Beat 3 of the page's arrival: seeded charcoal stains creep and then flood through the cream to the deckle, deepening where they overlap, and end on the crisp rect. The eye has more to watch than a cross-fade gives it.
cards.when: When we are trying to maintain continuity, connecting ideas, speaking across plates i think the cross-fade is the answer, when we are building an idea or introducing a new idea or looking to fill space to separate ideas, the soak is the transition.

author.key: `;field=soak` on a ledger page - or no field at all: the soak is the engine's own default

phases.name: the stains creep
phases.does: each seeded stain grows from its own lag on the field clock, deepening where two overlap
phases.trigger: the roll and the savor behind it (the scene's first frame on a mount)

phases.name: the ground closes
phases.does: the crisp charcoal rect takes over the last fifth, so the ground is flat before the title inks

lives.note: the soak branch of the field beat; the same stains are what the page's leave recedes

callable.why: implicit: the ground of every page that names no field

cards.when: When we are trying to maintain continuity, connecting ideas, speaking across plates i think the cross-fade is the answer, when we are building an idea or introducing a new idea or looking to fill space to separate ideas, the soak is the transition.
